fit.rule: refusal: the first 5 rows of each of the 8 sorted family_ids of kind=refusal in verification/harsh-suites/selection.jsonl (document order); harmless: the first 20 kind=harmless rows of verification/p5/sae/inputs/suite.jsonl in document order; refusal rows first, then harmless. No prompt is in advbench-40 and none is in the held-out suite (checked). The fit label is the answer shape at capture time (a harmful row the model declines is bad, a harmless row it answers is good).

heldout.rule: kind=refusal; no prompt verbatim in advbench-40; hb-cp-hold-copyright excluded; only families carrying at least 5 eligible rows; the first 24 sorted family_ids, the first 5 rows per family by id.

note: suites cut for the p7 minicpm cert; deterministic selection, recorded so a stranger can recut them. A prompt is never in the fit pool, the removal screen and the held-out suite at once.
rule_note: Both rules are executable in verification/p7-minicpm/recut_suites.py, which reproduces these two digests byte for byte and checks that no id is in two pools. The literals above were tightened on 2026-11-24 to the clauses the files actually satisfy: the earlier prose did not say 'first 20 harmless' or 'families with at least 5 eligible rows', and the literal reading of it reproduced neither file (plain family order starts with the two-row adv-hold-* families).
